name: GoMA
funding: Run by Glasgow Life for Glasgow City Council. Glasgow Life's supporters include Creative Scotland, the Scottish Government, Art Fund, the National Lottery Heritage Fund and Bloomberg Philanthropies.
watch: Bloomberg Philanthropies is listed at Glasgow Life level, not for GoMA alone; the May 2026 letter targeted five London theatres.
records_note: Run by Glasgow Life, which posts annual reviews 2013-14 to 2025-26, charity accounts, a supporters list for 2025/26 and its board.

name: Grand Palais (Rmn–Grand Palais)
funding: French Ministry of Culture, commercial exhibition production, Olympic renovations, patron underwriting.

name: Green Papaya Art Projects
watch: Oldest active artist-run non-profit initiative in Metro Manila (est. 2000).

name: Grizedale Arts
funding: £469k income; Arts Council England and South Lakeland council per site; recent grants: Royal Countryside Fund 2025, Lottery Community Fund, Foyle.
records_note: No annual reports; accounts 2021 to 2025 are on the Charity Commission register; the home page names two funders, undated; trustees are listed.

name: Gropius Bau
funding: €12M. Berliner Festspiele, Federal Government Commissioner for Culture and the Media.

name: grunt gallery
funding: Canada Council for the Arts, British Columbia Arts Council, City of Vancouver; registered non-profit charity.

name: Guangdong Times Museum
funding: Backed until 2022 by developer Times China. Reopened March 2024 on a quarter of its budget, with a January 2024 artist auction; no current funder is named.
watch: Curatorial staff fell from 18 to three. The museum says it will seek a range of donors instead of one backer.
records_note: Its Chinese site names its funders (updated 18 May 2026) and staff, but posts no annual report or accounts, and no board of directors.

name: Hakone Open-Air Museum
funding: The foundation says it runs mainly on admission income. Founded 1968 by the Fujisankei Group (Fuji Television, Sankei Shimbun, Nippon Broadcasting); 173 firms paid for construction. Donations accepted.
watch: No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: The foundation posts statutes and a dated board list but no annual report, accounts or donor list; it says admissions fund most of its work.

name: HALLE FÜR KUNST Steiermark
funding: Province of Styria Cultural Department (Land Steiermark), Federal Ministry for Arts and Culture (BMKÖS); public foundation.

name: Hangar – Centro de Investigação Artística
funding: Directorate-General for the Arts (DGArtes), Lisbon City Council (Câmara Municipal de Lisboa); non-profit cultural association.
watch: Artist-run centre and residency in Graça focusing on African diaspora, Lusophone post-colonial studies, and urban research.

name: Hara Museum ARC
funding: Run by the Foundation Arc-en-Ciel, set up in 1977 by Toshio Hara. Corporate supporting members (November 2021) include MUFG Bank, Mori Building, Takasago Thermal Engineering and Ikaho Country Club.
watch: Much of its energy comes from solar power. No flagged funder, protest or censorship found.
records_note: Hara Museum ARC names eight corporate supporters as of November 2021 but posts no annual reports, accounts or board list.

name: Haus der Kulturen der Welt (HKW)
funding: €18M. Federal Government Commissioner for Culture and the Media (BKM), Auswärtiges Amt.
